answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may trade, then use random cross-checks and community challenges to detect agents that coordinate or submit inconsistent claims. Proven Sybil identities lose their bonds through automatic slashing, while honest identities recover them and build reputation. Thus an attacker must finance one bond per fake agent and risk losing the entire bundle when a juniper, ferrous, or canyon test exposes coordinated behavior, making mass forgery economically unattractive.
